content: Trypan Blue is an ophthalmologic agent approved by the FDA for use in posterior segment eye surgeries, particularly to assist in the removal of epiretinal tissue. It is commonly used during vitrectomy procedures to stain epiretinal membranes, thereby facilitating their visualization and removal. The product is marketed under the brand name MembraneBlue™ 0.15%. Administration Instructions: Before using MembraneBlue™ 0. To prime the syringe, either retract the plunger or twist it clockwise into the stopper until it is tight, then continue turning until the stopper rotates freely within the syringe. Prior to injecting the dye, a fluid-air exchange should be performed, which involves filling the vitreous cavity with air to prevent dilution of the dye. The dye is then carefully applied to the retinal membrane using a blunt cannula attached to the syringe. Care must be taken to avoid contact between the cannula and the retina to prevent damage. The dye stains the membrane upon contact, and any excess dye should be removed from the vitreous cavity before performing an air-fluid exchange to prevent unnecessary spreading. Alternatively, MembraneBlue™ 0.15% can be injected directly into a balanced salt solution (BSS)-filled vitreous cavity instead of under air. Clinical experience has shown that sufficient staining occurs within 30 seconds of application in a BSS-filled cavity, provided the vitreous and posterior hyaloid have been completely removed. The dye is applied directly to areas where membranes are suspected, and it stains only the portions of the membrane that come into contact with it. The dye does not penetrate the membrane. Dosage Forms and Strengths: MembraneBlue™ 0.15% is supplied as a sterile ophthalmic solution in 2.25 mL syringes, each filled to a volume of 0.5 mL. Each mL of the solution contains 1.5 mg of trypan blue, along with sodium mono-hydrogen orthophosphate, sodium di-hydrogen orthophosphate, sodium chloride, and water for injection. The solution has a pH of 7.3–7.6 and an osmolality of 257–314 mOsm/kg. Contraindications: MembraneBlue™ 0.15% is contraindicated in cases where a non-hydrated (dry state), hydrophilic acrylic intraocular lens (IOL) is planned for insertion, as the dye may be absorbed by the IOL and cause staining. Warnings: Excessive staining can occur if the dye is not promptly removed from the eye after injection. It is essential to remove all excess dye to minimize the risk of unintended staining of ocular structures. Adverse Reactions: Clinical trials have reported adverse reactions such as discoloration of high-water-content hydrogen intraocular lenses and inadvertent staining of the posterior lens capsule and vitreous face. These stains are generally self-limited and resolve within one week. Use in Specific Populations: Pregnancy: Trypan blue is classified as Pregnancy Category C. Animal studies have shown teratogenic effects, including neural tube, cardiovascular, vertebral, tail, and eye defects, as well as increased post-implantation mortality and decreased fetal weight. In monkeys, trypan blue caused abortions at high doses but did not increase birth defects. There are no adequate studies in pregnant women, and the drug should only be used if the potential benefit outweighs the risk to the fetus. Nursing Mothers: It is unknown whether trypan blue is excreted in human milk. Caution is advised when administering the drug to nursing women. Pediatric Use: The safety and efficacy of trypan blue have been established in pediatric patients based on well-controlled studies. Geriatric Use: No significant differences in safety or efficacy have been observed between elderly and younger patients. Nonclinical Toxicology: Trypan blue has been shown to be carcinogenic in rats, with subcutaneous administration leading to the development of lymphomas. It was also mutagenic in the Ames test and caused DNA strand breaks in vitro. Mechanism of Action: MembraneBlue™ 0.15% selectively stains epiretinal membranes and internal limiting membranes during posterior segment eye surgeries, aiding in their visualization and removal. Storage: MembraneBlue™ 0.15% should be stored at temperatures between 15–25°C (59–77°F) and protected from direct sunlight. Additional Information: There is limited data on drug interactions, use in patients with renal or hepatic impairment, and use in immunocompromised individuals. The drug is supplied in sterile, single-use syringes and is intended for intravenous administration during ophthalmic procedures.
